MBE Growth of Superconductors.title: Enhanced Superconductivity in Multilayer FeSe Films by Simplified Molecular Beam Epitaxy
MBE Growth of Superconductors.authors: Maria Hilse, Zhe Chen, Jessica Lorraine Thompson, Kalana Dasunpriya Halanayake, Seong H Kim, Hemian Yi, Danielle Reifsnyder Hickey, Cui-Zu Chang, Nitin Samarth, Roman Engel-Herbert
MBE Growth of Superconductors.abstract: Multi-unit-cell (UC) β-FeSe films grown on SrTiO3(100) continue to attract attention because of the significant enhancement in the superconducting transition temperature (Tc) compared to that in bulk FeSe. In prior reports of molecular beam epitaxy (MBE)-grown β-FeSe/SrTiO3(100), elaborate growth protocols have been used to achieve enhanced Tc, leading to a general belief that careful pre-treatment of the SrTiO3 substrate and post-growth annealing in ultrahigh vacuum (UHV) are essential. Here, we report a greatly simplified protocol for the MBE growth of superconducting multi-UC β-FeSe films on SrTiO3(100), eliminating the need for careful substrate pre-treatment and post-growth UHV annealing while still achieving an enhanced Tc. With appropriate capping, epitaxial films with 14 UC thickness exhibit a zeroresistance transition temperature Tc ~ 20 K in ex situ electrical transport measurements. The MBE optimization process is guided by the growth-parameter dependencies of film morphology and structural properties, as characterized by reflection high-energy electron diffraction, X-ray diffraction, atomic force microscopy, and scanning transmission electron microscopy.

MBE Growth of Superconductors.title: Nanocrystalline cubic boron arsenide growth on GaAs(100) by gas source molecular beam epitaxy
MBE Growth of Superconductors.authors: Matthew A. Delmont, Yu Wu, Han-Hsuan Wu, Xiaoqing Pan, Christopher J. Palmstrom, Bolin Liao
MBE Growth of Superconductors.abstract: Cubic boron arsenide (c-BAs) is a promising ultrahigh thermal conductivity semiconductor, but its direct synthesis on lattice-mismatched substrates remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate the synthesis of nanocrystalline c-BAs thin films on GaAs(100) substrates using gas source molecular beam epitaxy. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals an optimal growth temperature window of 250-400 C to maintain near stoichiometry and suppress severe arsenic loss. Surface and structural characterizations via atomic force microscopy, reflection high-energy electron diffraction, and grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction demonstrate a Volmer-Weber 3D island growth mode and a preferential crystallographic alignment with the GaAs substrate. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy confirms a chemically sharp interface without gallium interdiffusion into the c-BAs layer. These findings establish an initial step for the integration of c-BAs into advanced thermal and optoelectronic platforms.

Superconductor-Semiconductor Interfaces.title: Ferroelastic domain wall driven glassy dynamics and photoresponse in a SrTiO$_3$ (111) two-dimensional electron gas
Superconductor-Semiconductor Interfaces.authors: Jyotirmay Maity, Manav Beniwal, Pranab Hazra, Sumit Tomar, Srimanta Middey
Superconductor-Semiconductor Interfaces.abstract: The (111) orientation of SrTiO$_3$ (STO)-based heterostructures has emerged as a versatile platform for two-dimensional electron gases (2DEGs), yet the influence of STO's polar ferroelastic domain-wall (DW) network on charge transport remains largely unexplored. Here we study AlO$_x$/STO (111) interfaces hosting 2DEGs of different carrier densities. In the lower-density 2DEG, low-temperature transport exhibits thermal hysteresis, slow resistance relaxation, cooling-rate dependence, and memory effects, signaling glasslike electron dynamics. The relaxation is strongly non-monotonic in temperature, increasing below $\sim$80 K, peaking near 25 K, and vanishing below $\sim$12 K, tracking the established evolution of the ferroelastic DW state of bulk STO rather than any electronic energy scale, which identifies the DW network as its origin. These signatures are absent in a second, more metallic interface with much higher carrier density, demonstrating that the electron-DW coupling can be tuned. We further show that polar DWs govern the photoresponse: the persistent photoconductivity rises sharply below $\sim$80 K, coinciding with the onset of DW polarity. Together, these results establish polar ferroelastic DWs as a carrier-density-tunable electronic degree of freedom in STO (111)-based 2DEGs, opening routes to manipulate 2DEG properties through topological defects.

Superconductor-Semiconductor Interfaces.title: Electric-Field Tunable Spin Texture in Dual-Gated HfS2/Graphene van der Waals Heterostructures
Superconductor-Semiconductor Interfaces.authors: Haozhe Yang, Zhendong Chi, Eoin Dolan, Josep Ingla-Aynés, Beatriz Martín-García, Witold Skowroński, Marco Gobbi, Andrey Chuvilin, Luis E. Hueso, Fèlix Casanova
Superconductor-Semiconductor Interfaces.abstract: Spin–charge interconversion provides the essential link between spin information and electrical signals in spintronic devices. In spin–orbit coupled systems, spin–charge interconversion can contain multiple components associated with different spin-polarization directions, reflecting the underlying spin texture. Tuning this spin texture, therefore, provides a way to control not only the magnitude of spin–charge interconversion but also the balance among its different components. Graphene-based van der Waals heterostructures provide an attractive platform for this purpose because interfacial spin–orbit coupling can host multiple spin–charge interconversion channels that couple to different spin-polarization directions. Here, we demonstrate electric-field control of spin texture in a dual-gated HfS2/graphene van der Waals heterostructure, where independent control of carrier density and vertical electric field allows us to disentangle electrostatic doping from electric field-induced spin–orbit effects. Nonlocal spin precession measurements show that, near zero vertical electric field, spin–charge interconversion is dominated by a spin Hall component with out-of-plane spins. Increasing the vertical electric field enhances additional in-plane spin components with Rashba–Edelstein-like character, including contributions both parallel and perpendicular to the charge current. These results provide experimental evidence that a vertical electric field can reconfigure the effective spin texture and control the corresponding spin–charge interconversion components, demonstrating electrical tunability of spin–orbit functionalities.

Superconductor-Semiconductor Interfaces.title: Effect of Annealing on Maze Domains in Topological Insulator - Magnetic Multilayer Heterostructures
Superconductor-Semiconductor Interfaces.authors: Benjamin A. Brereton, Soumyarup Hait, Christy J. Kinane, Francesco Maccherozzi, Ahmet Yagmur, Satoshi Sasaki, Thomas A. Moore, Sean Langridge, Christopher H. Marrows
Superconductor-Semiconductor Interfaces.abstract: Combining topological insulators with chiral magnetic multilayers offers the opportunity to greatly enhance the spin-orbit torque (SOT) driven manipulation of hosted spin textures, however this also exposes devices to the often poor temperature stability of the commonly used, Bi$_2$X$_3$-based (X is a chalcogenic element), topological insulator films. In this work we demonstrate through in-situ-annealing and polarised neutron reflectometry that the multilayer at a Bi$_2$Se$_3$ interface remains magnetically robust up to a temperature of 350 $^{\circ}$C: even as the Bi$_2$Se$_3$ epilayer structurally deteriorates. Through x-ray photoemission electron microscopy, an intermediate annealing temperature of $\sim$ 200 $^{\circ}$C was found to improve the domain ordering of the multilayer, allowing for field-induced skyrmion nucleation, all whilst sustaining minimal damage to the topological insulator

Nanowire Selective Area and Template-Ass.title: Quantum Interference Enhanced Rectification in Mesoscopic Nanowires
Nanowire Selective Area and Template-Ass.authors: T. J. Osborne, B. Braunecker, H. F. Legg
Nanowire Selective Area and Template-Ass.abstract: Nanoscale nonreciprocal elements are needed to control signal flow in scalable quantum technologies, but existing nonreciprocal components are often bulky. Here, we show that a strongly nonreciprocal current-voltage relation can arise entirely from coherent elastic scattering in a mesoscopic Rashba nanowire with gate-defined scatterers. We first identify the symmetry constraints that enforce reciprocal transmission in a phase coherent conductor even when inversion and time-reversal symmetry are broken. We then show how gates that are capacitively coupled to the leads, together with a magnetic scatterer or transverse subband mixing, can remove these constraints. In the weak-scattering regime, nonreciprocal conductance originates from interference between distinct backscattering paths. In the strong-scattering regime, nonreciprocity can be resonantly enhanced by the hybridization of the transmitting channel with bound states that arise from a higher transverse subband or spin-split band. In this regime, we find that a bias-induced change in the gate potentials of about one percent can produce an order-unity diode response, i.e., electrons are transmitted almost as in a clean wire for one bias polarity, whereas for the other polarity the current is strongly suppressed.

Nanowire Selective Area and Template-Ass.title: Nanowire-Assisted Epitaxial Lateral Overgrowth of Planar GaN(0001) on Diamond(100)
Nanowire Selective Area and Template-Ass.authors: Brijmohan Paramanik, Mayur Shinde, Subhranshu Sekhar Sahu, Soumyadip Chatterjee, Prajwal Pandey, Anshul Jain, Himanjal Bhattacharyya, Alpesh Donga, Apurba Laha
Nanowire Selective Area and Template-Ass.abstract: GaN-on-diamond heterostructures are promising for high-power and high-frequency electronics, however, direct epi- taxial growth on diamond (100) remains challenging due to severe lattice and thermal mismatches, which induce high threading dislocation densities. To overcome this challenge, we have used Plasma Assisted Molecular Beam Epitaxy (PAMBE) to grow wurtzite GaN layers on diamond(100) substrates using nanowire-assisted epitaxial lateral overgrowth (ELOG). Two nanowire templates (NW100, NW600) were benchmarked against a nanowire-free reference (NW000). High-resolution XRD, φ -scans, (0002) pole figures, and reciprocal space mapping show that NW100 attains the lowest dislocation density (5.51 x 10-4 nm-2) and microstrain (2.736 x 10-3), the narrowest (0002) reflection, and a c-axis lattice parameter (5.1821 Å) within 0.06% of the bulk value; NW000, in contrast, exhibits a contracted c-axis (5.1633 Å) and elevated dislocation density (6.26 x 10-4 nm-2), consistent with residual tensile stress. Cross-sectional TEM con- firms the intended diamond/AlN/nanowire/ELOG/planar-GaN layer sequence and shows threading dislocations bending into near-lateral trajectories, directly evidencing defect filtering by the nanowire template. Together, these results estab- lish nanowire-assisted ELOG as an effective strategy to suppress dislocation propagation and recover near-bulk lattice parameters in GaN-on-diamond heteroepitaxy, providing a structurally well-defined platform for device integration.

Nanowire Selective Area and Template-Ass.title: Spin-Dependent Transport in One-Dimensional Mercury- and Silver-Mediated DNA Nanowires
Nanowire Selective Area and Template-Ass.authors: Arpan De, William Livernois, Simon Vecchioni, Yoel P. Ohayon, M. P. Anantram
Nanowire Selective Area and Template-Ass.abstract: Metallo-DNA nanowires serve as a versatile, programmable scaffold for molecular-scale electronics. In this work, we demonstrate that periodic heavy-metal coordination fundamentally reshapes the electronic landscape of DNA, generating dispersive, metal-centered conduction bands rather than isolated localized states. Driven by enhanced inter-layer coupling, where second nearest-neighbor hopping plays a crucial role: the conduction bandwidth can approach 1 eV, more than double that of canonical DNA. These broad bands suggest enhanced robustness of transport against structural fluctuations. As a result of relativistic effects, in these quasi-one-dimensional materials, spin-orbit (SO) coupling enhances band dispersion and governs spin-dependent transport. We predict that although ligand hybridization reduces atomic SO splitting, the effective SO splitting in these nanowires is comparable to the next-nearest-neighbor hopping strength, which results in considerable spin mixing. We find that Hg2+-coordinated nanowire exhibit pronounced spin-flip conductance comparable to spin-conserving conductance across the LUMO manifold. This efficient spin conversion remains robust over extended molecular lengths and is accompanied by a set of highly delocalized unoccupied states with oscillating nodal structures, readily accessible under low-bias transport measurements. In contrast, the Ag+-coordinated nanowires exhibit weak spin-flip scattering that is more than an order of magnitude smaller than spin-preserving transport. This duality establishes the choice of coordination metal as a decisive parameter to govern metal-metal interaction, electron delocalization, and spin-dependent transport. Overall, our findings demonstrate how relativistic effects and quantum confinement intersect in these bio-templated, quasi-one-dimensional molecular conductors.

Nanowire Selective Area and Template-Ass.title: Pixelated Tellurium Nanowire Assemblies for Flexible and Polarization-Driven Multimodal Anticounterfeiting
Nanowire Selective Area and Template-Ass.authors: Yingtao Zhao, Hao Liu, Jiajun Liu, Shiyu Liu, Zhenhua Yang, Jinshi Zhao, Jian Zhu
Nanowire Selective Area and Template-Ass.abstract: Anticounterfeiting technologies capable of enabling both visual authentication and machine-readable encryption are critically demanded. Here we present a wafer-scale and flexible tellurium nanowire (TeNW) platform with programmable localized orientation, enabling dual-mode anticounterfeiting based on polarization-encoded information. By employing a lock–shear and lift-off strategy, pixelated and highly aligned TeNW arrays with feature sizes down to 5 μm are realized on arbitrary rigid and flexible substrates, exhibiting dichroic ratios of up to 4.6 and stretchability exceeding 100%. Beyond passive optical security, the semiconducting nature of TeNWs allows these oriented arrays to function as active channels in asymmetric Schottky photodetectors, delivering broadband photoresponse (405–1064 nm), an anisotropic photocurrent ratio of 2.35, and an ultrafast response time of 430 μs under self-powered operation. Leveraging this capability, polarization-encoded information can be transduced into polarization-sensitive electrical signals, establishing a hardware-level security paradigm that physically encodes information in the material rather than in algorithms.

Nanowire Selective Area and Template-Ass.title: Complementary Metal-Oxide Semiconductor-Compatible Phototransistor Platform for Neuromorphic Broadband Vision
Nanowire Selective Area and Template-Ass.authors: Zhongyu Liu, Zhenghao Xu, Li Zheng, Xuetong Zhou, Lingyan Shen, Xinhong Cheng, Zhijun Ning
Nanowire Selective Area and Template-Ass.abstract: Photodetection and neuromorphic computing promises sensing at the edge, yet most optoelectronic synapses lack spectral breadth or scalable silicon integration. Here we report a dual-gate synaptic transistor integrating colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) with a silicon-on-insulator (SOI) channel in a complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS)-compatible platform. This architecture synergistically combines the SOI channel for efficient charge transport and signal amplification with the CQD layer serving a dual role as a broadband absorber (300–1700 nm) and a charge-trap medium. The device exhibits a responsivity of 639 A W–1 and specific detectivity exceeding 3 × 1012 Jones at 1550 nm, parallelly emulating short- and long-term plasticity, multilevel conductance tuning, and highly programmable synaptic dynamics. The top gate enables reversible potentiation and depression, and self-powered operation supports low-power sensing and light-driven learning. We demonstrate system-level utility in a synaptic array that achieves pattern recognition with peak accuracy exceeding 96%, establishing a pathway to silicon-integrated, energy-efficient neuromorphic vision.

Nanowire Selective Area and Template-Ass.title: Multi-Terminal Reconfigurable Silver Nanowire Network for Associative-Learning-Like Response and Path Optimization
Nanowire Selective Area and Template-Ass.authors: Jiawen Qiu, Kun Wang, Wei Huang, Hao Su, Yongai Zhang, Xiongtu Zhou, Tailiang Guo, Chaoxing Wu
Nanowire Selective Area and Template-Ass.abstract: Emulating associative-learning-like responses and hardware-state-guided path optimization using reconfigurable physical networks offers a promising route toward adaptive neuromorphic hardware. Herein, a multiterminal reconfigurable Ag nanowire network is presented. This network exhibits a honeybee-inspired associative learning response and provides experimentally measured conductance states for ant colony pathfinding simulations. By employing a multielectrode array to deliver synchronized odor-like and nectar-like electrical stimuli, the network dynamically reconfigures its conductance pathways in a training-dependent manner. Following training, the postsynaptic current increases by 2 orders of magnitude after the first learning cycle and reaches a sustained suprathreshold level after three cycles, demonstrating that the device can simulate long-term memory consolidation. Software simulations further show that the experimentally measured Ag NW learning states can modulate a handwritten digit recognition model through a hardware-derived memory gate, enabling conditioned-stimulus-only recognition to improve progressively during associative learning. Furthermore, specific stimulation protocols reconfigure the conductance pathways of the Ag NW network, and the resulting hardware conductance states are used as weighting factors in ant-colony-inspired software simulations. With these hardware-derived weights, the simulated optimal path length is reduced from 1643.54 units to 1415.18 units, corresponding to an improvement of approximately 14% in path-search efficiency. This study highlights the potential of integrating reconfigurable physical networks with bioinspired algorithms, offering a hardware-software codesign platform for future adaptive neuromorphic systems.

Nanowire Selective Area and Template-Ass.title: Strain-Induced Interfacial Bond Evolution and Facet-dependent Strain Response of Electronic Properties in Oxidized Silicon Nanowires
Nanowire Selective Area and Template-Ass.authors: Yasir Mahmood, Daniel Wines, Viviana Dovale-Farelo, Kamal Choudhary, Lucas M Hale
Nanowire Selective Area and Template-Ass.abstract: Silicon nanowires (Si NWs) have emerged as promising candidates for next-generation nanoelectronic devices due to their tunable electronic properties, and compatibility with aggressive scaling requirements. The integration of strain further enhances their performance by modulating carrier mobility, band structure, and transport behavior without altering material chemistry. Within the NW, the silicon-silicon dioxide (Si-SiO$_{2}$) interface serves as a critical region where strain redistribution and suboxide bonding collectively influence the mechanical and electronic response. Here, we combine reactive force field molecular dynamics and first-principles calculations to investigate how oxidation-induced interfacial structure and crystallographic facet orientation govern strain-dependent bond evolution and facet-dependent strain response of electronic properties in oxidized Si NWs. Simulated dry thermal oxidation generates chemically realistic Si-SiO$_{2}$ interfaces, enabling direct characterization of bond order redistribution and stress gradient development across the interface under tensile strain. Interfacial Si-Si bonds exhibit elongation and reduced bond order associated with partial oxidation states, leading to localized stress concentration and preferential bond rupture. Complementary density functional theory calculations on facet-specific models reveal that orientation-dependent interfacial bonding modulates facet-dependent strain response of electronic properties. Together, these results establish a direct coupling between interfacial suboxide chemistry, mechanical deformation, and electronic structure, providing atomistic insight into strain-modulated behavior at oxidized silicon interfaces in faceted NWs.

Nanowire Selective Area and Template-Ass.title: Intracavity stimulated-emission amplification of fluorescence quenching for ultrasensitive Cd2+ detection in a single nanowire laser
Nanowire Selective Area and Template-Ass.authors: Xiaohong Shen, Zhitao Mao, Yilong Zhou, Lingxiao He, Mengyi Yu, Yan Liu, Yipei Wang, Xiaoqin Wu, Yi Xu
Nanowire Selective Area and Template-Ass.abstract: Micro/nano lasers offer a promising alternative to fluorescent probes for sensing applications. Semiconductor nanowires (NWs) can naturally serve as laser cavities, enabling enhanced light–matter interaction at the single-NW level. However, most reported NW lasers rely on environmental refractive-index changes, which are not applicable to heavy metal ion detection dominated by quenching. Here, we propose a lasing-based sensing mechanism in single NWs toward ultrasensitive heavy metal ion detection and experimentally demonstrate it using Cd2+ as a proof-of-concept target. Through a modified lasing rate-equation model, we elucidate the intracavity stimulated-emission amplification for quenching-induced perturbations, supported by experimental validation including the light in–light out curves, threshold variations, and fluorescence lifetime measurements. Ultrasensitive Cd2+ detection is experimentally demonstrated with a lowest tested concentration of 25 pg/ml. As a general performance benchmark, this value is approximately 9.8-fold to three orders of magnitude lower than those reported for conventional fluorescence methods. These results may extend the application of single NW lasers toward a compact platform for quenching-based sensing.

Nanofabrication and Cleanroom Processes.title: Effect of oxygen plasma treatment on the structural and superconducting properties of atomic-layer-deposited NbN thin films
Nanofabrication and Cleanroom Processes.authors: Nitesh Yerra, Mustafa Teke, Felix Otto, Marco Diegel, Detlef Born, Uwe Hübner, Nan Du, Mario Ziegler, Sahitya Varma Vegesna, Heidemarie Krüger
Nanofabrication and Cleanroom Processes.abstract: Surface oxidation is a common concern for ultrathin NbN superconducting devices, yet which superconducting properties it affects has not been established for films grown by plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition. We expose NbN films about 11.4 nm thick to an O$_2$ plasma for 0 to 60 s, which oxidizes the surface without etching the film, and characterize the same sample series by X-ray diffraction, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and transport measurements on 500 nm wide nanowires. XPS of the surface and the underlying layer shows that the plasma converts the surface to Nb$_2$O$_5$, whereas the bulk of the treated film is chemically identical to that of the untreated film. Crystalline $δ$-NbN remains intact. During exposure, the total film thickness rises and saturates between 40 and 60 s, indicating self-limiting surface oxide growth. The normal-state resistivity rises by 21% (dc) and 25% (optical) with the plasma dose, while the critical temperature and transition width are unchanged. The switching current densities of 4.9-6.2 MA/cm$^2$ at 4.2 K show no systematic dependence on the plasma dose. Their temperature dependence follows the dirty-limit depairing current of Kupriyanov and Lukichev, and the extrapolated switching currents reach 39-46% of the depairing current calculated from the optical resistivity and diffusion coefficient, in agreement with the width dependence reported for nanowires from the same process. The oxygen signature is confined to temperatures near $T_c$, where the supercurrent of the treated wires vanishes at least 0.5 K earlier than that of the untreated wire, consistent with a partially oxidized surface layer that acts on the film by the proximity effect. At these doses, oxygen narrows the temperature range of the supercurrent from above but does not systematically reduce the low-temperature current-carrying capacity of the wires.

Nanofabrication and Cleanroom Processes.title: Frequency improvement and asymmetry characteristics of tri-stripe AlGaN/GaN MSM-2DEG varactors
Nanofabrication and Cleanroom Processes.authors: Gengxin Lin, Lingfeng Kang, Zejia Deng, Jianzhong Chen, Qiyu Chen, Jianxin Ning, Yukun Han, Junze Li, Jianping Zeng
Nanofabrication and Cleanroom Processes.abstract: This study presents an AlGaN/GaN heterojunction varactor employing a tri-stripe metal–semiconductor–metal (MSM) structure that exploits the two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG). The device exhibits a strong dependence of its electrical characteristics on the device width (W): both series resistance and capacitance decrease monotonically with reducing W. Through dimensional scaling, the R0·Cj product of the device decreases significantly, thereby improving the cutoff frequency (fc). Although the capacitance switching ratio (Cratio) shows a slight decrease with reduced W, the overall cutoff frequency figure-of-merit (FOM) of the device is effectively improved. Specifically, using a tri-stripe MSM-2DEG structure with a width of 10 μm and a gate gap of 450 nm, a high FOM of 8.27 THz and a Cratio of 3.42 are obtained. The study further reveals that the capacitance characteristics become asymmetric for smaller W values. Concurrently, the shift voltage (Vshift) shifts toward lower voltages with decreasing W, corresponding to the point of most rapid capacitance change, where the Fermi level (Ef) aligns with the conduction band (Ec) minimum. This phenomenon is closely related to the reduction in 2DEG concentration at the AlGaN/GaN interface, likely attributed to enhanced etching-induced damage during size scaling. The 2DEG concentration vs bias exhibits a transition from linear decay on both sides when Ef is far from Ec minimum, to exponential decay near Vshift region—representing a “linear–exponential–linear” evolution. Furthermore, the fabrication process of the device is significantly simplified—all electrodes can be formed in a single step via electron beam lithography.

Nanofabrication and Cleanroom Processes.title: Impact of oxidation conditions in SiO2 atomic layer deposition on interface state densities at β -Ga2O3 (001) MOS interfaces with 600 °C post-deposition annealing
Nanofabrication and Cleanroom Processes.abstract: We investigated the impact of SiO2 film deposition conditions in either thermal or plasma-enhanced atomic layer depositions (ALDs) on the interface characteristics of β-Ga2O3 metal–oxide–semiconductor (MOS) capacitors, especially focusing on oxidation reaction conditions in ALD. The formation of the interface with an interface state density as low as ∼1011 eV−1 cm−2 at 0.2 eV below the conduction band edge and a low near-interface oxide trap density was achieved by tuning the O3-dose in thermal-ALD, with a post-deposition-annealing temperature limited to a relatively low temperature of 600 °C to avoid the thermally induced damages on Ga2O3. The fixed charge density at the SiO2/β-Ga2O3 interface was also minimized by thermal-ALD with the sufficient dose of O3. These results demonstrate the significant role of the control of SiO2 deposition conditions to achieve high-quality SiO2/β-Ga2O3 MOS interfaces with low-thermal-budget processes.

Nanofabrication and Cleanroom Processes.title: Modification of optical properties in ultrathin ALD-grown NbN layers using oxygen plasma treatment
Nanofabrication and Cleanroom Processes.authors: Mustafa Teke, Nitesh Yerra, Alireza Sadeghi, Mario Ziegler, Detlef Born, Nan Du, Marco Diegel, Uwe Hübner, Sahitya V. Vegesna, Heidemarie Krüger
Nanofabrication and Cleanroom Processes.abstract: NbN thin films with a nominal thickness of 10 nm were grown by atomic layer deposition (ALD) on Al$_2$O$_3$-buffered Si substrates and treated with oxygen plasma for 0 s (untreated), 20 s, 40 s, and 60 s to investigate oxygen-induced changes in their optical properties. Spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) measurements were performed before and after oxygen plasma treatment over the ultraviolet-visible-near-infrared (1.24-6.20 eV) and infrared (0.041-0.827 eV) spectral ranges. Film thickness determined by X-ray reflectivity (XRR) was used as a fixed parameter in the optical modeling to extract the dielectric function, optical constants, and effective free-carrier concentration. We observed the emergence of a distinct absorption feature near 4.9 eV following oxygen plasma treatment, consistent with the oxidation of the NbN surface and the resulting change in its optical properties. Increasing the treatment time from 0 to 60 s reduced the effective carrier concentration from $1.20 \times 10^{22}$ to $1.03 \times 10^{22}$ cm$^{-3}$ and the effective carrier mobility from 2.44 to 2.27 cm$^2$ V$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$. The obtained results provide a basis for understanding the effects of oxygen plasma treatment on NbN thin films.

Nanofabrication and Cleanroom Processes.title: Confinement Drives Valley Splitting above 4 K in Buried Silicon Quantum Wells
Nanofabrication and Cleanroom Processes.authors: Davide Degli Esposti, Emma C. Brann, Asser Elsayed, Davide Costa, Mark Friesen, Giordano Scappucci
Nanofabrication and Cleanroom Processes.abstract: Controlling the energy scales of a quantum system is essential for defining robust qubits. In silicon, the nearly degenerate conduction-band valleys create a leakage channel from the single-spin computational basis. Here, we perform spectroscopic measurements of single- and two-electron states in buried silicon quantum wells. Across a linear array of four quantum dots with an average orbital energy of 2.4(2) meV, we report an average single-electron valley splitting of 0.40(6) meV and an average two-electron singlet–triplet splitting of 0.24(7) meV. In three dots, we observe a strong correlation between valley splitting and orbital energy, with an average linear coefficient of ≈0.22 (meV/meV). In contrast, the remaining dot exhibits the highest valley splitting of 0.76(2) meV and low correlation. Our findings show that strong confinement can effectively enhance valley splitting in buried quantum wells, thereby establishing a viable path toward shuttling and sparse-occupation-based architectures in low-disorder heterostructures.

Nanofabrication and Cleanroom Processes.title: Localization of hexagonal boron nitride color centers using patterned dielectric layers on graphene
Nanofabrication and Cleanroom Processes.authors: M. K. Prasad, V. Babenko, A. W. Tadbier, S. Hofmann, J. P. Goss, J. D. Mar
Nanofabrication and Cleanroom Processes.abstract: One of the most promising building blocks for the development of spin qubits, single-photon sources, and quantum sensors at room temperature, as well as 2D ultraviolet light-emitting diodes, is defect color centers in 2D hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). However, a significant requirement for the realization of such devices toward scalable technologies is the deterministic localization of hBN color centers. Here, we demonstrate a novel approach to the localization of hBN color center emission by using patterned dielectric layers grown on graphene via atomic layer deposition (ALD). While color center emission is quenched within areas where hBN is transferred directly on graphene due to charge transfer, it is maintained where hBN is transferred on micrometer-sized Al2O3 pillars, which act as barriers to charge transfer. Importantly, our approach allows for device architectures where graphene layers are used as top and bottom electrodes for the application of vertical electric fields, such as for carrier injection in electroluminescent devices, Stark shifting of color center emission, and charge state control of defect color centers. Furthermore, the use of ALD to grow dielectric layers directly on graphene allows for the control of tunnel barrier thicknesses with atomic layer precision, which is crucial for many of these device applications. Our work represents an important step toward the realization of a wide range of scalable device applications based on the deterministic localization of electrically controlled hBN color centers.

Nanofabrication and Cleanroom Processes.title: Interface-enabled low-voltage SiO2 gating of VO2 nanobeams for large room-temperature resistance modulation
Nanofabrication and Cleanroom Processes.authors: Yanqing Zhang, Zonglei Zhang, Ning Qiu, Jiaqi Guo, Hanbin Zheng, Kaihan Shan, Fan Zhou, Yonglong Zhou, Shibin Yuan, Weiming Xiong
Nanofabrication and Cleanroom Processes.abstract: Three-terminal gating offers an effective strategy for modulating the electrical transport and metal-insulator transition (MIT) behavior of vanadium dioxide (VO2), while conventional SiO2-gated VO2 devices usually show limited gate tunability. Here, we demonstrate large low-voltage resistance modulation in VO2 nanobeams directly grown on SiO2/Si substrates. The direct-growth configuration establishes a distinct VO2/SiO2 interfacial configuration in a Si-compatible back-gated device geometry. At room temperature, the channel resistance is reduced by approximately 75% under a gate voltage of only 3 V, corresponding to an electric field of 0.1 MV cm−1. When the device is biased near the MIT temperature, the same gate voltage triggers a gate-assisted transition, leading to a current increase of more than two orders of magnitude and a resistance modulation above 99%. In contrast, transferred VO2 nanobeam devices exhibit negligible gate-induced modulation even under much higher gate voltages, supporting an important role of the direct-growth-enabled VO2/SiO2 interfacial configuration in the enhanced gate response. These findings suggest that interfacial engineering may provide an effective route for improving the gate tunability of SiO2-gated VO2 devices, with potential for low-voltage, Si-compatible correlated-oxide electronics.

Germanium and Sn-Ge Epitaxy.title: NTL amplification in a SuperCDMS-style detector fabricated from a University of South Dakota-grown germanium crystal
Germanium and Sn-Ge Epitaxy.authors: Dongming Mei, Gerardo Gonzalez, William Baker, Mark Platt, Nader Mirabolfathi
Germanium and Sn-Ge Epitaxy.abstract: Neganov-Trofimov-Luke (NTL) amplification enables eV-sub-keV detection thresholds for low-mass dark-matter and coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering experiments. We evaluated two University of South Dakota (USD)-grown germanium crystals fabricated as SuperCDMS-style four-channel athermal-phonon detectors and operated near 10 mK. The crystals had electrically active impurity concentrations near $10^10~\mathrm^-3$ and etch-pit densities of $300$-$7000~\mathrm^-2$. Contact-free biasing produced no resolvable amplification. However, after depositing a 600 nm aluminum bias contact, Detector~2 exhibited clear voltage-dependent NTL gain. The reconstructed channel-B energy increased from approximately 3.9 keV at 0 V to 34.9 keV at 40 V, corresponding to an 8.9-fold enhancement. Statistical centroid uncertainties were below 0.3%, while low-bias fits yielded effective prompt- and NTL-phonon response coefficients of $(6.77\pm0.82)%$ and $(4.77\pm0.20)%$, respectively, excluding systematic uncertainties. These results demonstrate the feasibility of USD-grown germanium for SuperCDMS-style high-voltage phonon detectors and highlight the importance of both crystal quality and contact fabrication in achieving NTL amplification.

A cumulative exposure of 4.69 × 10 22 protons on target yielded a total number of observed counts of 124 − 12 + 14 and a flux-averaged cross section of 0.98 ± 0.10 ( statistical ) ± 0.10 ( systematic ) relative to the standard-model expectation of 5.9 × 10 − 39 cm 2 . This information is used to improve constraints on nonstandard neutrino interactions mediated by heavy particles.

Single Junction and Sn-Based Devices.title: Mitigating self-doping effect enables efficient tin-based perovskite light-emitting diodes
Single Junction and Sn-Based Devices.authors: Chaohui Liang, Xiaofei Zhang, Hongxi Chen, Zhidan Liu, Sheng Wang, Lingmei Kong, Xuyong Yang, Lin Wang
Single Junction and Sn-Based Devices.abstract: Tin (Sn)-based perovskites are promising eco-friendly candidates for next-generation displays, owing to their excellent optoelectronic properties and low-cost solution processability. However, the performance of Sn-based perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs) is hindered by uncontrolled crystallization and facile Sn2+ oxidation, leading to poor film morphology and high defect density. Herein, we propose a multifunctional hydroxyurea (HU) buried interface to regulate the crystallization kinetics and optoelectronic properties of Sn-based perovskites. The hydrophilic NH2 groups of HU establish a hydrogen-bond network with the perovskite halide ions, which enhances precursor wettability and increases the initial nucleation density to facilitate the growth of uniform, dense, and pinhole-free perovskite films. Furthermore, the C=O groups of HU can coordinate with uncoordinated Sn ions and effectively inhibit their oxidation. Moreover, the suppression of Sn2+ oxidation helps mitigate the Sn4+-induced self-doping effect, thus upshifting the valence-band maximum and reducing the hole injection barrier. Consequently, the optimized PeLED exhibits pure-red emission (620 nm) and achieves a maximum external quantum efficiency of 12.8%.

Josephson and Proximity Effects.title: Phase engineering of odd parity state in a quantum dot Josephson junction
Josephson and Proximity Effects.authors: Shohei Kobayashi, Tyler Lindemann, Sergei Gronin, Geoffrey Gardner, Peter Stano, Daniel Loss, Michael Manfra, Seigo Tarucha, Sadashige Matsuo
Josephson and Proximity Effects.abstract: Controlling fermion parity in quantum-dot Josephson junctions (QDJJs) enables access to novel superconducting physics. While parity transitions are usually tuned electrically, we study phase-induced transitions in a strongly coupled QDJJ using the superconducting phase difference across the dot terminals, denoted by $φ$. We find that this phase allows control over the ground state parity, with parity transitions observed as the Andreev bound states (ABSs) energies crossing zero. These crossings occur near $φ= π$, and their behavior is in good correspondence to a simple model considering a single-level quantum dot proximitized by a superconductor. These results place phase-controlled QDJJ arrays as a promising platform for exploring exotic phenomena such as Majorana zero modes.

Josephson and Proximity Effects.title: Edge-localized supercurrent transport in Josephson junctions with Al/Ni multilayer barriers
Josephson and Proximity Effects.authors: Ivan P Nevirkovets, Mikhail A Belogolovskii, John B Ketterson
Josephson and Proximity Effects.abstract: The survival and reorganization of supercurrents in strongly scattering media remains a fundamental question at the intersection of condensed matter physics and quantum transport. We investigate the propagation of superconducting correlations in metallic multilayers consisting of alternating nanometre-thick Al and Ni layers. Earlier investigations we conducted on Josephson junctions containing (Al/Ni)n multilayers demonstrated SQUID-like magnetic interference patterns, suggesting supercurrent localization at the device edges despite the diffusive nature of the metallic weak link. This work reports the results of a study demonstrating that the characteristics of devices incorporating Al/Ni multilayers are markedly influenced by differing boundary conditions along their sidewalls. Specifically, we consider junctions fabricated using three sidewall insulation methods: (i) anodization only, (ii) a combination of anodization and SiO2 deposition, and (iii) SiO2 deposition only. Solely devices fabricated using anodization exhibited oscillatory interference patterns. Further, to distinguish between intrinsic quantum-coherent edge states and trivial surface shunting mechanisms, we fabricated hybrid Josephson devices in which a standard Nb/Al/AlOₓ/Al/Nb tunnel junction was either embedded in or connected in series with Al/Ni multilayer structure. Unlike pure multilayer junctions, these hybrid devices exhibited conventional Fraunhofer-type interference patterns, indicating that charge carriers, after passing the edges of the multilayer structure, are redistributed deep into the bulk of the adjacent superconducting electrode. The obtained results are consistent with a strongly edge-weighted supercurrent distribution in Al/Ni multilayer Josephson junctions. Although the microscopic origin of this boundary-dominated transport remains unresolved and requires further study, these structures provide a useful platform for investigating how superconducting correlations propagate in strongly scattering magnetic multilayers.

Josephson and Proximity Effects.title: Magnetization and Josephson current coupling drives the Josephson diode effect in FeTe0.55Se0.45 van der Waals junctions
Josephson and Proximity Effects.authors: Seung-Hyun Shin, Cheong-Eung Ahn, Chang-Won Choi, Taekoo Oh, Si-Young Choi, Genda Gu, Gil Young Cho, Gil-Ho Lee
Josephson and Proximity Effects.abstract: The Josephson diode effect (JDE) reflects symmetry breaking in the current-phase relation (CPR) of Josephson junctions, yet establishing its microscopic origin is often challenging. We investigate the mechanism of the JDE in van der Waals Josephson junctions based on FeTe0.55Se0.45, a platform where superconductivity, topology, and magnetism may coexist at the interface. Our devices exhibit a robust zero-field diode response with asymmetric switching currents. Magnetic-field measurements reveal a hysteretic Fraunhofer pattern and magnetic-resonance-induced voltage feature, evidencing interfacial magnetism coupled to the Josephson current. Microwave response further shows half-integer Shapiro steps with asymmetric evolution, demonstrating contributions from both a second harmonic and a magnetization-induced phase shift in CPR. Numerical simulations combining magnetization dynamics and Josephson phase dynamics reproduce these features, confirming that the JDE originates from interfacial coupling between magnetization and Josephson current. This work provides a transport-based route to pinpoint the microscopic mechanism of the JDE, establishing a platform for exploring magnetically active interfacial superconductivity, and enables the design of nonreciprocal superconducting devices in clean, interface-engineered van der Waals systems.

Josephson and Proximity Effects.title: Josephson effect in symmetry-mismatched van der Waals hybrid junctions of NbSe2-Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x and NbSe2-Bi2Sr2-xLaxCuO6+y
Josephson and Proximity Effects.authors: Yuying Zhu, Ziye Liu, Hongtao Yan, Lin Zhao, Xingjiang Zhou, Qi-Kun Xue, Ding Zhang
Josephson and Proximity Effects.abstract: Coupling superconductors of different symmetries may lead to emergent quantum phenomena but experimental studies on heterojunctions made of lattice-mismatched crystals are scarce. Here, we fabricate Josephson junction by van der Waals stacking NbSe2 flakes on freshly cleaved surfaces of Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x or Bi2Sr2-xLaxCuO6+y. We obtain pronounced Josephson currents across the heterojunctions at temperatures below 7 K. The Josephson coupling strength, characterized by the product of the critical Josephson current I_c and the normal state resistance R_n, can reach about 0.3 mV, much exceeding the values previously reported in Pb-Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x or Nb-Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x junctions. Microwave irradiation induces integer Shapiro steps. We also observe the Fraunhofer diffraction pattern by applying an in-plane magnetic field. We compare our results with the theoretical calculations that take into account the coherent tunneling and the order parameter mixing. Our work demonstrates the hybrid junctions as a distinctive platform for addressing pairing symmetry and emergent quantum phenomena.

Josephson and Proximity Effects.title: Scanning gate microscopy modulation of supercurrent in graphene Josephson junctions
Josephson and Proximity Effects.authors: Ivan Villani, Samuele Fracassi, Niccolò Traverso Ziani, Maura Sassetti, Matteo Carrega, Vaidotas Mišeikis, Camilla Coletti, Fabio Beltram, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Sergio Pezzini, Stefan Heun
Josephson and Proximity Effects.abstract: Graphene Josephson junctions (JJs) represent an excellent platform for quantum technologies, thanks to the combination of high carrier mobility, ballistic transport, and gate-tunable critical currents, preserved even under quantizing magnetic fields. Investigating the spatial distribution of supercurrent flow could be crucial for elucidating transport mechanisms and advancing the engineering of these devices. In this work, we employ a scanning gate microscope to investigate supercurrent transport in hexagonal boron nitride-encapsulated graphene JJs. We study the supercurrent modulation as a function of tip voltage bias and tip-to-sample distance and provide a complete characterization of the tip-induced modulation. Our experimental results are quantitatively consistent with numerical simulations and pave the way toward local mapping and manipulation of gate-tunable superconducting phenomena with unprecedented spatial resolution.

Josephson and Proximity Effects.title: Transparency-controlled multiple charge transfer in superconducting junctions with local shot-noise scanning tunneling spectroscopy
Josephson and Proximity Effects.authors: Yudai Sato, Maialen Ortego Larrazabal, Jian-Feng Ge, Ingmar Swart, Doohee Cho, Wolfgang Belzig, Juan Carlos Cuevas, Milan P. Allan, Jiasen Niu
Josephson and Proximity Effects.abstract: Charge transport in superconducting junctions at finite voltages is governed by Andreev reflections, including multiple Andreev reflections, which are processes that enable multiple charge transfer, a hallmark that shot noise can directly quantify. Since the effective charge extracted from shot-noise measurements varies with the transparency of the junction, systematic control of transparency is essential but experimentally challenging. Here, we present shot-noise scanning tunneling microscopy measurements enabled by a newly developed amplifier, allowing access to different transparency regimes. We perform shot-noise measurements on Pb(111) with tunable transparency at 2.2 K and observe that the shot noise evolves from a single-electron tunneling regime to multiple charge-transfer regimes as transparency increases. Our results are quantitatively consistent with theoretical simulations of Andreev reflections and multiple Andreev reflections for a single-channel system. These results establish junction transparency as the key parameter governing the evolution of charge transport and demonstrate that noise STM is a powerful platform for investigating microscopic charge transport mechanisms with controlled junction transparency at the atomic scale.

Josephson and Proximity Effects.title: Resist-Free Shadow Deposition Using Silicon Trenches for Josephson Junctions in Superconducting Qubits
Josephson and Proximity Effects.authors: Tathagata Banerjee, Stephen Daniel Funni, Saswata Roy, Judy J. Cha, Valla Fatemi
Josephson and Proximity Effects.abstract: Superconducting qubit fabrication innovations continue to be explored to achieve higher performance. Despite improvements to base layer fabrication and processing, resist-based Josephson junction (JJ) schemes have largely remained unchanged. The polymer mask during deposition causes chemical contamination and limits in situ and ex situ surface preparation, junction materials, and scalability. Here, we demonstrate a resist-free approach to junction fabrication based on etched silicon trenches that is compatible with standard silicon microfabrication processes and easily integrated into existing innovations in qubit base layer fabrication and chemical processing. We fabricate Al-AlOx-Al JJs and qubits using this method, measuring median energy relaxation times up to 188 μs. We find minimal contamination at the substrate–metal interface and fluctuations of energy relaxation on a 45 h time scale that are narrow and normally distributed. The method widens the process window for substrate preparation and new materials platforms.

Josephson and Proximity Effects.title: Superconducting parametric amplifiers based on arrays of unequal Josephson junction elements
Josephson and Proximity Effects.authors: Boris Chesca, Tom Dixon, Narendra Acharya, Renuka D. Pothuraju, Jacob W. Dunstan, Connor D. Shelly, Oscar W. Kennedy
Josephson and Proximity Effects.abstract: Impedance matching is a crucial feature of an amplifier used to increase its instantaneous bandwidth and is typically achieved using static LC resonators. Here we show an approach to impedance matching in parametric amplifiers using arrays of unequal Josephson-junction-based elements (rf/dc SQUIDs, SNAILs, etc). The elements act either as small-footprint flux-tunable inductors forming an impedance-matching circuit, or 'active' amplifier elements which result in amplifier gain. We develop an analytical theory describing these systems, predicting a quasi-non-periodic amplifier frequency and gain modulation with applied flux and the broadening of gain bandwidths. We demonstrate this in devices using arrays of flux-focused SNAILs where flux biasing varies across the array. We find instantaneous bandwidths of 200 MHz with $>$17 dB of gain centred at $\sim$5.4 GHz in a device without a static impedance matcher. This broadening of amplifier bandwidth is stable with $>$100 MHz bandwidth at 17 dB gain across $>$1.2 GHz tunable bandwidth. Our analytical model captures flux dependence and qualitatively reproduces gain-bandwidths giving confidence in our understanding of these systems and allowing operational figures of merit to be optimised in future devices.

Josephson and Proximity Effects.title: Finite-Temperature Transconductance of Multiterminal Josephson Junctions with Topological Andreev Spectra
Josephson and Proximity Effects.authors: Gleb S. Seleznev, David C. Ohnmacht, Wolfgang Belzig
Josephson and Proximity Effects.abstract: Multiterminal Josephson junctions (MTJJs) provide a controllable platform for engineering topological Andreev spectra. At zero temperature, Andreev bound states (ABSs) with nonzero Chern numbers give rise to quantized transconductance between superconducting terminals. We derive the finite-temperature transconductance of MTJJs using linear-response theory. We first demonstrate the destructive role of temperature: changes in the thermal occupations of the ABSs destroy exact transconductance quantization. We then show that finite temperature can also play a constructive role by making the transconductance sensitive to finite-energy topological crossings hidden from the zero-temperature response. Our results establish the thermal limitations of transconductance quantization and identify finite-temperature transport as a probe of otherwise inaccessible topology in Andreev spectra.

Josephson and Proximity Effects.title: Rashba-controlled emergence and reversal of critical-field anisotropy in p-wave magnet--superconductor hybrids
Josephson and Proximity Effects.authors: Rui-Xiang Cheng, Zhao Gong, Dong-Hui Xu, Chui-Zhen Chen
Josephson and Proximity Effects.abstract: We show that tuning Rashba spin-orbit coupling can change the in-plane field direction along which an $s$-wave superconductor is most susceptible to Zeeman depairing. We consider a two-dimensional $s$-wave superconductor subject to an odd-parity exchange field induced by a $p$-wave magnet. Without Rashba coupling, the out-of-plane exchange field enhances the in-plane critical field but leaves its angular response exactly isotropic, despite the anisotropic magnetic spin texture. Minimizing the Bogoliubov--de Gennes grand potential over uniform singlet pairing, we find that increasing Rashba coupling first generates and then reverses the principal-axis critical-field contrast, switching the minimum-critical-field direction by $90^{\circ}$. Equal principal-axis fields at the intervening compensation point coexist with residual angular modulation. We interpret the reversal through competing momentum-dependent depairing contributions from the magnetic and Rashba spin textures, while the on-site singlet pairing channel remains unchanged. Direction-dependent discontinuous collapses of the order parameter further shape the critical-field curves. These results identify a tunable directional paramagnetic response within the uniform-pairing sector. In heterostructures with sufficient electrostatic tunability of interfacial Rashba coupling, this reversal would enable gate control of the easy-depairing axis without reorienting the magnetic texture.

Josephson and Proximity Effects.authors: Paul Corbae, Alex Abelson, Shivani Srivastava, Heemin Lee, Bevin Huang, Lyrik R-J Lee, Davis B. Rash, Cheng-Tai Kuo, Donghui Lu, Mihir Pendharkar, Loren D. Alegria, Tian T. Li, Keith G. Ray, Shannon P. Harvey, Apurva Mehta, David I. Schuster, Vincenzo Lordi, Paul B. Welander, Jun-Sik Lee
Josephson and Proximity Effects.abstract: Decoherence remains a critical obstacle to achieving high-fidelity, scalable superconducting qubits, with the tunnel barrier of Josephson junctions a key source of loss, yet the microscopic structure of this buried layer has remained difficult to probe experimentally. Here, we use resonant x-ray reflectivity to resolve the coordination environments within the AlO x barrier of Al / AlO x / Al Josephson junctions as a function of oxidation conditions. We find that the barrier coordination evolves from more tetrahedral toward octahedral character with increasing oxidation pressure, while the lower metal-oxide interface is comparatively undercoordinated and disordered relative to the upper interface. Comparison with simulated x-ray absorption spectra identifies the dominant coordination motifs within the oxide and at its interfaces, providing depth-resolved structural insight that informs microscopic models of two-level system formation. These results link growth conditions, local coordination environments, and junction electronic properties, providing a materials-level foundation for interpreting how the tunnel barrier influences coherence in superconducting qubits.

Josephson and Proximity Effects.title: Decoupling Josephson Coupling and Supercurrent Nonreciprocity in Twisted NbSe2/NbSe2 van der Waals Junctions
Josephson and Proximity Effects.authors: Seung-Gi Lee, Kwon-Neong Jung, Jae-Keun Kim, Jae-Chun Jeon, Jiho Yoon, Stuart S. P. Parkin, Kun-Rok Jeon
Josephson and Proximity Effects.abstract: The microscopic origin of supercurrent nonreciprocity in van der Waals Josephson junctions remains under debate, particularly regarding the role of twist-angle engineering. Here, we investigate twisted NbSe2/NbSe2 vertical Josephson junctions with controlled crystallographic alignment and clean interfaces. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy directly determines the twist angle and interface quality. While Josephson coupling exhibits a pronounced twist-angle dependence, the supercurrent diode efficiency remains small and shows no systematic angular dependence. In contrast, enhanced diode responses emerge in weakly coupled junctions with reduced transparency and interfacial disorder. Deliberate interface degradation further enhances the diode efficiency to nearly 30% and produces irregular magnetic-field dependence. These results demonstrate a clear decoupling between Josephson coupling and supercurrent nonreciprocity, indicating that interfacial disorder rather than twist-angle-controlled momentum matching plays a dominant role in the observed diode response. Our findings establish an important benchmark for understanding nonreciprocal superconducting transport in van der Waals Josephson devices in the future.

Josephson and Proximity Effects.title: Field-free superconducting diode and tunable vortex dynamics in NbN/FePt stripe-domain heterostructures
Josephson and Proximity Effects.authors: Juan C. Zapata, Emilio De Biasi, Martin Sirena, Jeehoon Kim, Nestor Haberkorn
Josephson and Proximity Effects.abstract: We demonstrate reconfigurable, field-free superconducting diode behavior in NbN/FePt and NbN/AlN/FePt heterostructures with remanent stripe domains in the FePt layer. NbN films 10 nm thick are capped either directly with FePt or through a thin AlN spacer, which reduces electronic proximity effects while preserving magnetic coupling through stray fields. At zero applied magnetic field, the superconducting diode efficiency reaches approximately 50--60% in NbN/FePt when the stripes are perpendicular to the current and is strongly reduced when they are parallel. The diode effect persists in NbN/AlN/FePt with efficiencies reaching approximately 35--40%, supporting a magnetic origin of the nonreciprocity. We interpret the response as asymmetric vortex transport in the remanent magnetic landscape, with preferential edge vorticity and a Lorentz force that favors inward flux injection or outward motion depending on current polarity. Under applied perpendicular magnetic fields, the interplay between the external field and the magnetic stray fields modifies the flux-flow instability and the apparent instability velocity inferred from transport, with values below those reported for bare NbN films. These results show that stripe-domain ferromagnetic overlayers provide a reconfigurable route to control superconducting nonreciprocity and flux-flow stability in NbN-based heterostructures.

Josephson and Proximity Effects.title: Optical signatures of Rashba--Dresselhaus coupling across Franz--Keldysh and Landau regimes in two-dimensional semiconductors
Josephson and Proximity Effects.authors: Bahruz Suleymanli, Samir Tariverdiev, B. Tanatar
Josephson and Proximity Effects.abstract: We develop a unified theory of the interband optical response of a two-dimensional semiconductor with simultaneous Rashba and Dresselhaus spin-orbit couplings in electric and magnetic fields. In crossed fields, the in-plane electric field generates an effective spin-orbit drift field that modifies the Landau spectrum and spinor states, while at zero magnetic field the problem maps onto Landau--Zener spin dynamics.At zero external fields, the total joint density of states above the band gap remains unchanged, while characteristic subgap structures appear. Pure Rashba coupling produces an inverse square root singularity, whereas a finite Dresselhaus term gives a step and a logarithmic peak, allowing the two couplings to be distinguished optically. At zero magnetic field, the Franz--Keldysh response shows a crossover from diabatic to adiabatic spin dynamics as the electric field is reduced. In the weak-field Rashba regime, the field-free singularity becomes a finite peak whose height scales as $\mathcal E^{-1/3}$ and whose position approaches $E_g-E_{\rm SO}$, providing a direct measure of the Rashba energy. In a perpendicular magnetic field, spin-orbit coupling shifts and splits the Landau absorption lines and produces anticrossings without changing their total weights. The Rashba splitting changes from a $\sqrt{B}$ dependence at weak fields to a linear dependence at strong fields. Finally, in crossed electric and magnetic fields, the electric field broadens the Landau lines and drives a continuous crossover toward the Franz--Keldysh regime, while spin-orbit coupling produces opposite shifts and different widths for the two members of each doublet.

Josephson and Proximity Effects.title: Electric-field tunable spin texture in dual-gated HfS$_2$/graphene van der Waals heterostructures
Josephson and Proximity Effects.authors: Haozhe Yang, Zhendong Chi, Eoin Dolan, Josep Ingla-Aynés, Beatriz Martín-García, Witold Skowroński, Marco Gobbi, Andrey Chuvilin, Luis E. Hueso, Fèlix Casanova
Josephson and Proximity Effects.abstract: Spin-charge interconversion provides the essential link between spin information and electrical signals in spintronic devices. In spin-orbit coupled systems, spin-charge interconversion can contain multiple components associated with different spin-polarization directions, reflecting the underlying spin texture. Tuning this spin texture therefore provides a way to control not only the magnitude of spin-charge interconversion, but also the balance among its different components. Graphene-based van der Waals heterostructures provide an attractive platform for this purpose because interfacial spin-orbit coupling can host multiple spin-charge interconversion channels that couple to different spin-polarization directions. Here, we demonstrate electric-field control of spin texture in a dual-gated HfS$_2$/graphene van der Waals heterostructure, where independent control of carrier density and vertical electric field allows us to disentangle electrostatic doping from electric field-induced spin-orbit effects. Nonlocal spin precession measurements show that near zero vertical electric field, spin-charge interconversion is dominated by a spin Hall component with out-of-plane spins. Increasing the vertical electric field enhances additional in-plane spin components with Rashba-Edelstein-like character, including both parallel and perpendicular to the charge current contributions. These results provide experimental evidence that a vertical electric field can reconfigure the effective spin texture and control the corresponding spin-charge interconversion components, demonstrating electrical tunability of spin-orbit functionalities.

Josephson and Proximity Effects.title: Room-temperature multiferroicity in van der Waals Fe-doped SnSe semiconductors
Josephson and Proximity Effects.authors: Muhammad Younis, Sichao Dai, Anwar Ali, Shuang Pan, Nayab Arif, Muhammad Ahsan Iqbal, Wei Tang, Yuexing Chen, Hui Fang, Francis Chi-Chung Ling, Shahid Atiq, Haixin Chang, Yu-Jia Zeng
Josephson and Proximity Effects.abstract: Two-dimensional materials hosting multiple ferroic orders are highly desirable for next-generation electronic and spintronic technologies. However, achieving stable and tunable ferroic functionalities at room temperature remains a key challenge. Here, we report the growth of van der Waals (vdW) Fe-doped SnSe semiconductor that can be exfoliated down to thin layered flakes. These crystals exhibit tunable ferromagnetism well above room temperature, with the Curie temperature increasing from 342 to over 400 K through controlled Fe incorporation. In parallel, anomalous Hall measurements reveal interfacial spin polarization at the SnSe/Pt interface driven by magnetic proximity effects, enabling spin-dependent magnetotransport. Furthermore, robust ferroelectric behavior at room temperature is confirmed by piezoresponse force microscopy. Although the ferromagnetic and ferroelectric orders coexist within the same material system, they originate from distinct mechanisms without direct magnetoelectric coupling. The semiconducting nature of Fe-doped SnSe is supported by both theoretical and experimental analyses, which further enhances its multifunctionality. These results establish Fe-doped SnSe as a versatile vdW platform for integrating magnetic, electric, and electronic functionalities in future energy-efficient devices.

Majorana and Topological Superconductivi.title: Majorana physics in a Luttinger liquid with attractive interactions
Majorana and Topological Superconductivi.authors: Francesco Debortoli, Nitya Cuzzuol, Luca Barbiero, Fabian Grusdt
Majorana and Topological Superconductivi.abstract: Majorana zero modes are the hallmark of topological superconductivity. In one-dimensional systems, these zero modes are usually introduced in the context of gapped, mean-field models that do not conserve particle number, such as the Kitaev chain. By nonlocally encoding a conventional fermion across spatially separated Majorana zero modes, these systems become inherently immune to local decoherence. In this work, we show that signatures of Majorana edge physics persist in a number-conserving, gapless Luttinger liquid of spinless fermions with short-range attractive interactions. We identify the two-point correlator as a sharp diagnostic, revealing an edge-to-edge revival whose sign depends on the fermion-number parity. This revival is robust in the thermodynamic limit and persists in the excited states of the system and at different fillings. A simple particle-hole ansatz for the ground state of the system with an odd number of fermions captures the physics of the system for a wide range of interaction strengths, interpolating between the free-fermion limit and the strongly interacting Majorana regime. Finally, we propose a concrete protocol to realize this model with ultracold dipolar molecules or atoms in an optical lattice and to detect the revival via beam-splitter interferometry, opening an experimental route to Majorana physics beyond the conventional gapped-superconductor paradigm.

Majorana and Topological Superconductivi.title: Majorana Edge-to-bound State Transition in Interferometric Superconductor Rings
Majorana and Topological Superconductivi.authors: Xiangyu Bi, Aoshen Yang, Hongzi Cao, Ganyu Chen, Yuqiang Fang, Zeya Li, Qizheng Sun, Junwei Huang, Da Wang, Fuqiang Huang, Toshiya Ideue, Qianghua Wang, Yoshihiro Iwasa, Hongtao Yuan
Majorana and Topological Superconductivi.abstract: Manipulating flux quanta in topological superconductors is central to vortex braiding in quantum computing. Their interferometric superconducting rings can host either topologically protected edge states with fluxes confined inside the central hollow area or vortex bound states in flux cores at the annulus walls. Here we demonstrate a strategy to drive topological edge states into vortex bound states by tuning the relative scale of vortex size and annulus width in nano-ring interferometric device on 2M-WS$_2$ topological superconductor. Near its superconducting transition where the coherence length exceeds the annulus width, Little-Parks oscillations exhibit expected periods for flux bundles in ring-center, consistent with edge states residing at inner and outer rims of the annulus. Upon cooling, where the coherence length shrinks below the annulus width, the unexpectedly increased oscillation period reflects multiple fluxes distributed along annulus region in flux necklace configuration, implying a transition from extended edge states to localized vortex bound states. Ginzburg-Landau simulations and local density-of-states calculations with Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations reveal that large values for both Ginzburg-Landau parameter and flux-pinning energy are vital for such a transition. Our findings provide a novel strategy for understanding flux manipulation towards flux braiding and topological quantum computing.

Majorana and Topological Superconductivi.title: Suppressing Majorana Hybridization in Atomically Assembled Cr Chains on Bi2Pd
Majorana and Topological Superconductivi.authors: Jinkyung Kim, Piotr Kot, Ryo Ogawa, Atustaka Maeda, Andreas J. Heinrich, Nicolas Lorente, Deung-Jang Choi
Majorana and Topological Superconductivi.abstract: Magnetic-atom chains on superconductors can host Majorana zero modes, but in finite chains the two end modes generally hibridize and split away from zero energy. We show that Cr chains assembled atom-by-atom on the Bi-terminated surface of Bi2Pd enter a short-localization-length Shiba chain regime wthat strongly suppreesses this finite-size hybridization. Scanning tunneling spectroscopy reveals a chaing-leght-driven closing and reopening of the in-gap spectrum, followed by zero-bias modes localized at the chains ends. Green-function calculations reproduce the evolution and show an exchange of electorn-holec haracter across the transition. From the residual splitting we extract a localization length of about three atomic sites, explaining the stability of the zero-energy modes in experimentally accessible chains.

Majorana and Topological Superconductivi.title: Chiral topological superconductivity from quantum anomalous Hall states in ferromagnetic metals
Chiral Cavity Vacua as Local Generators and Probes of Non-Abelian Kitaev Topology
Majorana and Topological Superconductivi.abstract: We show how a gyrotropic cavity vacuum generates, probes, and spatially programs non-Abelian topology in the Kitaev honeycomb model. Gauge-consistent virtual-photon elimination produces a universal helicity-odd interaction $\mathrm{i}[P_x,P_y]$ alongside same-order even dressing. For the leading bond polarization, this commutator is exactly the Kitaev three-spin mass. Mode normalization imposes a thermodynamic constraint: one extended normalized mode gives a local mass that vanishes with sample area, whereas a localized mode writes a finite topological island and a finite mode density enables a bulk mass. The exact Majorana solution yields helicity-reversed Chern gaps and edge propagation, while integrated circular dichroism exactly measures the mass generator, $\langle\mathrm{i}[P_x,P_y]\rangle=-\sqrt3p^2\langle O_3\rangle$. Real-space calculations reveal a non-Abelian island and a helicity wall with two co-propagating Majorana modes. Uniform helicity reversal is a Dirac-mass quench with $n_{\rm ex}\proptoτ_Q^{-1}$, whereas moving a wall localizes the gap closing. The equilibrium vacuum kernel contains sum-frequency rather than resonant denominators. These results establish distinct criteria for local and bulk cavity-induced topology.

Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.title: Intrinsic Raman Modes and Crystal Symmetry of Altermagnetic $α$-MnTe
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.authors: Yunpeng Cui, Shuai Zhang, Jia-Liang Xie, Jinxuan Liang, Hao Lin, Miao Qin, Jiawei Shao, Gongling Chen, Yidian Li, Yixuan Luo, Deng Hu, Bingru Lu, Hao Li, Xiang Li, Tiantian Liu, Haodong Yu, Hongyun Zhang, Shuyun Zhou, Zhiwei Wang, Yanfeng Guo, Tiantian Zhang, Miao-Ling Lin, Ping-Heng Tan, Feng Jin, Luyi Yang
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.abstract: Crystal symmetry governs the physical properties of materials and provides the framework for interpreting their microscopic excitations and macroscopic responses. In altermagnets, the crystal symmetries that relate opposite-spin sublattices give rise to momentum-dependent spin splitting despite compensated magnetization. Determining the real crystal symmetry is therefore essential for understanding the intrinsic electronic and magnetic properties. For the altermagnetic semiconductor $α$-MnTe, conflicting Raman assignments have left both its intrinsic lattice excitations and its crystal symmetry unresolved. Here we combine high-resolution Raman and second-harmonic generation (SHG) spectroscopy with first-principles calculations to distinguish intrinsic lattice excitations from Te-derived spectral contributions and to examine bulk inversion symmetry of $α$-MnTe. We show that several prominent Raman features previously assigned to $α$-MnTe instead originate from segregated Te clusters or precipitates. The remaining intrinsic Raman response consists of a single Raman-active mode assigned to the calculated $E_{2g}$ phonon, consistent with the centrosymmetric $D_{6h}$ symmetry. The SHG response agrees with surface electric-dipole and bulk electric-quadrupole contributions expected for a centrosymmetric $D_{6h}$ crystal, supporting the preservation of bulk inversion symmetry in $α$-MnTe. Our findings revise the Raman assignments in $α$-MnTe and provide a basis for interpreting its altermagnetic properties within the appropriate crystal-symmetry framework.

Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.title: Ballistic transport and crystallographic control in altermagnetic quantum rings
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.authors: Edilberto O. Silva
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.abstract: We study coherent two-terminal transport through a finite-width $d$-wave altermagnetic quantum ring with nonmagnetic leads. A confined Aharonov--Bohm flux remains exactly $h/e$ periodic and, in the symmetric one-mode geometry, produces an exact half-flux transmission zero. A perpendicular field shifts the interference pattern according to an effective area $A_{\rm eff}=1.0342\,πr_0^2$ and the altermagnetic splitting resolves the common zero into nearby spin-dependent nodes. Rotating the crystal reverses the transmitted spin, whereas the mirror orientation $θ_A=π/4$ is exactly spin degenerate. For a $50$~nm reference ring, sub-tesla fields yield windows with $|P_T|>0.99$, the most accessible of which requires a uniform field alone and no confined flux. Finite-bias, thermal, disorder, Zeeman, and spin-conserving voltage-probe calculations show that the polarization is appreciably more stable than individual coherent-resonance amplitudes. These results identify interference-node positions, flux periodicity, and crystal-controlled spin polarization as experimentally useful signatures of an altermagnetic mesoscopic interferometer.

Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.title: Finite-width altermagnetic quantum rings: angular-channel hybridization and Aharonov--Bohm physics
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.authors: Edilberto O. Silva
Altermagnets and Novel Heterostructures.abstract: We study a finite-width two-dimensional quantum ring with a quadratic $d$-wave altermagnetic term, Tan--Inkson confinement, a perpendicular magnetic field, and independently tunable Aharonov--Bohm (AB) flux. The altermagnetic interaction mixes $m$ and $m\pm2$ angular channels while preserving their parity. Circular symmetry renders the crystal orientation spectrally irrelevant and makes the two spin blocks exactly isospectral. The resulting same-parity anticrossings are resolved at low filling, and multichannel mixing is found near the Fermi level of highly occupied rings. Independent converged calculations for $N_e=1400$ and $1800$ establish the reconstructed Fermi edge and magnetic response in a finite field window and the persistent current over a full AB flux period. The analytic conventional reference separates radial-subband depopulation (dHvA-type cycles) from finer finite-ring shell oscillations; we do not assign a global Fourier spectrum to unverified altermagnetic field scans. The few-electron thermal response is obtained from an exact fixed-particle-number canonical partition function, avoiding finite-system errors of a fixed-mean-number approximation. The circular model supports an equilibrium charge current but no persistent spin current.
